newsitem.title: UK: UK's C&W criticises U.S. telecom move.
newsitem.headline: UK's C&W criticises U.S. telecom move.

text.p: Proposals from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to try to force foreign carriers to reduce rates for international calls were not in the interests of customers or operators, British telecommunications company Cable & Wireless Plc said in a statement.

"The international accounting rate is only one strand in the fabric of international telecoms regulation," C&W said late on Thursday. "Any attempt to deal with accounting rates in isolation risks undermining the very existence of international telecoms services."
The FCC estimates that the move would have saved net outpayments from the U.S. to foreign carriers some $5.0 billion in 1995.
It also said U.S. consumers pay 99 cents a minute for international calls against 16 cents for domestic, despite the fact that costs are similar.
C&W noted that the United States had not adopted "piecemeal solutions" to deregulating its own market and should not do so in the international market.
"As competition opens in international telecoms, we hope the same breadth of vision will prevail," C&W said.
